assertions.name: d_pn is exactly the stated convex combination of d_pp and d_nn (sympy)
tr_2 being affine in d, z + d_pn lies STRICTLY between z + d_nn and z + d_pp
L = -log(z+d) is decreasing in d, so L_pp < L_pn < L_nn is forced
delta is nowhere near the value that would break convexity, so the ordering is not tunable by q
the one system that binds is assigned the MIDDLE bond constant
the deuteron itself is overshot by ~1.27x — the same defect seen a second way
the block's 6.29 MeV is reproduced, so the reading of it is right

description: The pn interface letter of convention D is exactly the convex combination (1/2 + delta/4) d_pp + (1/2 - delta/4) d_nn of the pp and nn letters, verified symbolically and at 200 bits. Since the two-strand trace is affine in the offset and L = -log(z+d) is strictly decreasing in it, L_pp < L_pn < L_nn is forced for every q and every delta in (0,2); delta at q0 is 0.0014 and would have to reach 2 (q = 3.458) to break convexity. But of the three two-body systems only pn binds, so a binding-ranking constant must put pn at an extreme, and a convex combination never is. The inversion measured at A=2 is therefore definitional, not numerical and not tunable. The corpus's np preference lives in the (2,2)|-4 Wigner term (6.2894 MeV, reproduced), which has no analogue at A=2. Caveat recorded: this L has no spin, and the bound/unbound split is a spin effect; the ORDER is not.
caveats: This arc's L carries no spin. The deuteron binds in the 3S1 triplet channel and every 1S0 two-body system is unbound, so a spinless bond constant cannot separate bound from unbound and is not claimed to. The finding is the ORDER, which the absence of spin does not explain.
wigner-np-pairing and reeb-pn-magnitude-criticality are read, not re-derived, and neither is contradicted. Nothing here concerns A >= 3, where other channels exist.
The alpha = m_e/(q0(q0-1)) normalisation is the sibling's, taken as-is; the ordering conclusion is independent of it, since alpha > 0 is a common factor.
